correctness.rationale: Modulo 3 f(x)=x^3≡x. In zero class f=x(x²−3) increases ν3 by exactly 1 before hitting k; hence H=k−ν3,k(x). For ρ=±2 exact identity f(x)−ρ=(x−ρ)(x+ρ/2)²: a=ν3,k(x−ρ),b=ν3,k(x+ρ/2), first jump to a+2b, then b=1 and valuation rises exactly 2 until k. Gives H=0 if a=k else 1+max(0,ceil((k−a−2b)/2)). Exact partition into a=b=1, a≥2/b=1, b≥2/a=1, and two exceptional roots gives stated polynomial; each modulus has 3 fixed points. Independently iterated every x for k=1..7 and matched pointwise formulas and sharp maximum depths. Infinite k conclusion follows exact valuation identities, not finite tests.
